name: Kakeibo
tagline: A local-only token budget diary that breaks down where every coding-agent session spent your quota.
description: Named after the Japanese household budgeting ledger, Kakeibo turns opaque coding-agent quota burn into an honest daily diary. Instead of guessing why a session exhausted your allowance in twenty minutes, you get a line-by-line accounting of where the tokens actually went.

The kakeibo CLI parses local session transcripts directly on your machine—separating resumed conversation history, verbose tool output, retry loops, and prompt-cache misses—without ever uploading prompts, code, or telemetry anywhere.

features.title: Four-column token spend breakdown
features.detail: Attributes every session's tokens across resumed context, raw tool stdout, failed-step retries, and cold prompt-cache misses.

features.title: Quota drain flags & culprit commands
features.detail: Highlights the exact tool invocations—unbounded grep dumps, full lockfile reads, or thrashing test loops—that spiked a session's cost.

features.title: Strictly local-only by design
features.detail: Reads local agent log directories offline into a compact local ledger with zero accounts, zero cloud sync, and zero outbound requests.

features.title: Daily & per-repo kakeibo summaries
features.detail: Roll up token spend by day, repository, or task branch so you can compare lean workflows against expensive ones.
